question.problem: Noah removes some food from his freezer to defrost. The temperature of the food was $-{4.6}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$ After a few hours, the temperature of the food increased by ${10.5}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$ What was the temperature of the food after those few hours?

current_example.problem: Nazareth is doing an experiment in her Chemistry class. She heated a liquid whose initial temperature was $-5.6^{\circ} \, \textrm{C}.$ After several minutes, the temperature of the liquid rose by $4.7^{\circ} \, \textrm{C},$ at which point she decided to end the experiment. What was the final temperature of the liquid?
current_example.worked_solution:
To determine the final temperature of the liquid, we add the change in temperature to the initial temperature of the liquid. This gives

$$
-5.6^{\circ}\,\textrm{C} + 4.7^{\circ}\,\textrm{C} = -0.9^{\circ}\,\textrm{C}.
$$

Therefore, the temperature of the liquid at the end of the experiment was $-0.9^{\circ}\,\textrm{C}.$
